title: Self-Hosted vs Hosted Salesforce MCP: How to Migrate Either Way
summary: Salesforce's DX MCP server reaches end of life on November 2, 2026. Compare self-hosted and hosted Salesforce MCP, and migrate in either direction.
body_markdown:
## Should you run a self-hosted or a hosted Salesforce MCP server?


**Short answer:** For business data, move to Salesforce's hosted MCP servers. They have been generally available for Enterprise Edition orgs and above since April 29, 2026. Salesforce runs them, and every call runs under the signed-in user's permissions. Keep a self-hosted server only where the hosted servers can't go, such as unattended agents, because the hosted servers support no service accounts. Self-hosting doesn't avoid the new meter: Salesforce bills registered agent calls over MCP and direct APIs alike.


*Timing matters: Salesforce's own DX MCP server reaches end of life on November 2, 2026. Facts checked October 24, 2026.*


## What are the options?


Option Who runs it Status


Salesforce hosted MCP servers (` sobject-reads` ,` sobject-all` , Data 360, and others) Salesforce GA since April 29, 2026 for Enterprise Edition and above


Salesforce DX MCP server (` @salesforce/mcp` ) You, on a laptop or server End of life November 2, 2026


Community servers, such as` smn2gnt/MCP-Salesforce` and` tsmztech/mcp-server-salesforce` You Open source (MIT), maintained by individuals


The DX server was built for developers: deploying metadata, running Apex tests, managing scratch orgs. Its` data` toolset also includes` run_soql_query` , which is why some teams pointed it at production data. The[endpoint guide](https://www.stacksync.com/blog/salesforce-mcp-server-endpoints-tools) covers what the hosted servers expose.


## How do self-hosted and hosted servers compare?


Self-hosted Salesforce hosted


Hosting and updates You run, patch, and secure it Salesforce runs it


Authentication Varies: CLI-authorized orgs, username and password, or OAuth client credentials OAuth authorization code flow with PKCE through an External Client App


Identity Often one shared integration identity The signed-in user, later a registered agent


Permissions Whatever the connecting identity can do Field-level security, object permissions, and sharing rules on every call


Unattended agents Possible with stored credentials Not supported: no service accounts or machine-to-machine flows


Tools Whatever the server's code exposes Fixed standard tools plus Flows, Apex, and API Catalog entries you publish


HPI metering Registered agent calls over the API are metered Registered agent calls are metered


Self-hosted vs hosted


## What changes on November 2 for the DX MCP server?


Salesforce posted the end-of-life notice on October 5, 2026. After November 2:


-


Salesforce stops maintaining it and ships no new releases.


-


The GitHub repositories become read-only archives.


-


The npm package is marked deprecated but stays installable, so pinned setups (version 0.30.15) keep working.


-


Salesforce delivers its developer tooling as skills instead, in the` forcedotcom/sf-skills` repository.


If you use it for metadata and testing, move to the skills on your own schedule. If you use it to query production records, move that work to the hosted servers. An unpatched local server holding production credentials is a liability.


## How do you migrate from self-hosted to hosted?


- 01


**Find every self-hosted server.** Check developer laptops and reps' AI clients for` @salesforce/mcp` and community packages, and check which orgs and users they authenticate as.


- 02


**Map the tools.**` run_soql_query` becomes` soqlQuery` on` sobject-reads` . Record writes move to` sobject-mutations` . Custom logic becomes a Flow or Apex tool you publish.


- 03


**Enable the servers.** Standard servers ship disabled. An admin turns each one on in Setup.


- 04


**Create the External Client App** with the` mcp_api` and` refresh_token` scopes and PKCE. Allow up to 30 minutes before it becomes available.


- 05


**Reconnect each client** to the server URL and sign in as the user. Test in a sandbox first, at the` /sandbox/` endpoint.


- 06


**Remove the old credentials.** Delete stored passwords and tokens from config files, and revoke the old app's access.


- 07


**Confirm the switch.** In event logs, hosted MCP traffic shows` API_CLIENT_CATEGORY` =` SALESFORCE_HOSTED_MCP` .


Connecting a client to the hosted server


## When should you go the other way?


Moving from hosted to self-hosted makes sense in one main case: an agent that runs with no user present, such as a nightly account-scoring job. The hosted servers need a signed-in user, so they can't serve it.


Before you build one, check two things. First, Salesforce's security guidance warns against building a custom proxy around its REST APIs in place of the hosted server. Second, if a model drives the job, it is still an agent: register it under Agentic Identity, and expect its API calls to be metered. See the[Agentic Identity checklist](https://www.stacksync.com/blog/salesforce-agentic-identity-checklist) .


Often the better fix is to take the agent off Salesforce for reads. A scheduled agent that scans thousands of accounts can query a synced database copy instead, and write back through a single Flow tool. Our guide to[moving agent reads to a synced database](https://www.stacksync.com/blog/migrate-salesforce-agent-reads-to-database) walks through it.
